column1: # Campaign 27 exact original-test evidence for the authenticated prepared point-read TCP route.

column8: note
The source contract keeps prepare and execute inside the existing authenticated command loop and typed packet framing; the historical receiver/framing regression matrix remains open.
Prepared registry creation occurs only after the existing handshake, authentication, and concrete session open; complete handshake capability compatibility remains open.
COM_STMT_PREPARE, COM_STMT_EXECUTE, and silent COM_STMT_CLOSE are connected to one per-connection typed registry; generic dispatch, all commands, and broad error parity remain open.
Prepared metadata, errors, and binary result packets retain the authenticated Protocol 4.1 negotiation; the complete capability-sensitive dispatch matrix remains open.
Prepared binary responses use the existing packet sequence and exact terminal result-set lifecycle; complete text-query terminal-NUL semantics remain open.
Prepared execution remains within the existing sequential worker-local connection session; wait-timeout and full session-variable behavior remain open.
Each prepared execute installs the existing real query cancellation authority before PD/TiKV execution; complete timeout, kill, and deadline behavior remains open.
Prepared execution reuses the existing listener drain, active-query cancellation, and worker join ownership; complete Go shutdown breadth remains open.
The prepared read path adds no process or transaction worker and stays under existing joins; commit wait groups and all write transactions remain unimplemented.
Prepared handles are created only after the existing native-password authentication and plugin negotiation; the full Go auth-plugin matrix remains open.
Prepared state is connection-local but COM_CHANGE_USER and its required statement cleanup and reauthentication behavior remain open.
Prepared dispatch begins after the existing authenticated identity is established; complete secondary-plugin negotiation remains open.
Prepared command payloads enter the same bounded PacketReader and the typed execute decoder rejects truncation before execution; the complete max-allowed-packet matrix remains open.
Prepare metadata and execute binary rows use negotiated EOF deprecation through protocol-owned encoders; complete OK/EOF compatibility and session-state tracking remain open.
Successful prepared executes receive the same connection and monotonically allocated query identities as text reads; full process-info publication and SQL text reporting remain open.
COM_STMT_CLOSE is silent and idempotently removes only the current connection's handle, and socket close drops the whole local registry; complete Go close behavior remains open.
Prepared executes remain within existing accepted/completed/failed connection accounting; complete Go command metrics and labels remain open.
Prepared state is created after the existing authenticated connection response and attributes parsing; complete connection-attribute behavior remains open.
Prepared support adds no health or listener authority and remains behind existing admission; the complete Go health contract remains open.
Prepared commands extend the existing sole listener rather than creating another endpoint; complete Go listener reinitialization behavior remains open.
Prepared execution inherits the existing idempotent admission stop and forced drain path; complete shutdown-flag behavior remains open.
No new server lifecycle branch is introduced for prepared statements, preserving admission-before-drain ordering; exact Go callback and health-publication behavior remains open.
Prepared reads retain one existing query cancellation lease and result-set close path during drain; broad graceful-shutdown integration remains open pending the real live proof.
The registry is an ordinary connection-local value and prepared results use the existing finish/close cleanup; broad socket, statement, and goroutine leak detection remains open.
Prepared commands remain inside one existing connection lease and do not create secondary sessions; complete status and per-user counting remains open.
Prepared handles are owned below the already-admitted authenticated connection and do not alter its exactly-once release; complete per-user limit behavior remains open.
